title: Finite intersection of a central diagonalizable subgroup with the derived group
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $C\subseteq G$ be a central closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], where central means commuting with every element after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Assume that $C$ is diagonalizable: $C\simeq D_F(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Here $F[M]$ has basis $e_m$, multiplication $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$, and Hopf operations $\Delta(e_m)=e_m\otimes e_m$, $\epsilon(e_m)=1$, $\iota(e_m)=e_{-m}$. Let $G^{\mathrm{der}}$ be the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism $(x,y)\mapsto xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ factors [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-derived-subgroup]. Then the scheme-theoretic intersection $C\cap G^{\mathrm{der}}$ is finite over $F$, meaning that its coordinate algebra is finite-dimensional over $F$. Neither reductivity of $G$ nor smoothness or connectedness of $C$ is assumed; the conclusion holds also for nonreduced $C$ in positive characteristic.

source.place: Proposition 12.46(a), printed pp.245--246, its faithful-representation weight-block determinant argument extended from a central torus to a central diagonalizable subgroup; Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, pp.234--235, supply arbitrary diagonalizable weight decompositions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-central-torus-faithful-weight-blocks] to $H=G$ and its trivial central subgroup $T=\mathbf G_m^0$. This is a closed subgroup: on affine coordinates its identity inclusion is the surjective counit $F[G]\to F$. Its centrality is the identity law. The node applies to every affine finite-type $H$, hence gives a nonzero finite-dimensional $V$ and a closed-immersion homomorphism $\rho:G\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(V)$. Keep only this conclusion, not its torus weight blocks.

source.place: Theorem 4.9 and Corollary 4.10, p.87; Proposition 12.46(a), p.246, first choice of a faithful representation.

proof.text: Restrict $\rho$ to $C\simeq D_F(M)$ and apply [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-representation-weight-grading]. Enumerate its nonzero weight spaces as $V_1,\ldots,V_s$, with characters $\chi_i$; put $d_i=\dim_F V_i>0$. For $g\in G(A)$, centrality of $C$ says that $\rho_A(g)$ commutes with $C(B)$ for every $A$-algebra $B$. The commutant clause of that node implies that it preserves each $V_i\otimes_F A$; the same holds for $g^{-1}$. Choosing bases of the $V_i$ therefore makes $\rho$ block diagonal over every $A$. Restriction to the $i$th block gives a group-scheme homomorphism $\rho_i:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V_i)$: its entries are the corresponding entries of $\rho$, and its inverse is the block of $\rho(g^{-1})$. On $C$, this block is $\chi_i$ times the identity.

source.place: Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, pp.234–235; Proposition 12.46(a), p.246, centrality and weight blocks, using all algebra-valued points.

proof.text: The determinant homomorphism of [def-sc-general-linear-group] defines $\delta_i=\det\circ\rho_i:G\to\mathbf G_m$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-derived-subgroup], $\delta_i$ is trivial on $G^{\mathrm{der}}$, since $G$ has exactly the smoothness, connectedness and affine finite-type hypotheses of that node and $\mathbf G_m$ is commutative affine. On $C$ its value is $\chi_i^{d_i}$, by the determinant formula for a scalar $d_i\times d_i$ matrix. Thus on the scheme-theoretic intersection $K=C\cap G^{\mathrm{der}}$ the restricted invertible function $a_i=\chi_i|_K$ satisfies $a_i^{d_i}=1$. This is an identity of functions, not merely an equality on $F$-points.

source.place: Proposition 12.46(a), p.246, determinant-one argument; replace its point argument by the scheme-level character-vanishing property of the derived group.

proof.text:
The intersection $K$ is the closed subscheme of $G$ cut out by the sum of the ideals of $C$ and $G^{\mathrm{der}}$ [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Consequently the coordinate map $F[\operatorname{GL}(V)]\to F[K]$ is surjective: first use the closed immersion $\rho$, then quotient by this sum of ideals. In the block basis, every matrix coordinate restricts to $0$ or one of the $a_i$. The determinant restricts to $\prod_i a_i^{d_i}=1$, so its inverse restricts to $1$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Thus the $a_i$ generate $F[K]$ as an $F$-algebra. The relations from step 3 yield a surjection
$$F[t_1,\ldots,t_s]/(t_i^{d_i}-1:1\le i\le s)\longrightarrow F[K],\qquad t_i\longmapsto a_i.$$
Reduce every exponent modulo its positive $d_i$. The finitely many monomials $\prod_i t_i^{b_i}$ with $0\le b_i<d_i$ span the source, hence their images span $F[K]$. It is therefore finite-dimensional (indeed of dimension at most $\prod_i d_i$), proving finiteness. No division by $d_i$, reducedness of $C$ or $K$, or reductivity of $G$ occurred.

source.place: Proposition 12.46(a), p.246, final scalar-matrix bound; explicit coordinate quotient retaining nonreduced roots of unity.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 12.46(a), p.246, extended to arbitrary central diagonalizable subgroup schemes by Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, pp.234–235; coordinate quotient replaces finiteness of rational points.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q37-f4be81578 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Milne iAG2017 Thm 12.12 (a)=>(b),(d), Rem 12.13 (printed pp.234-235) and Prop 12.46(a) with its proof (pp.245-246). Milne's 12.46(a) is for a central torus and argues by rational points. The delivery replaces that with a coordinate-algebra argument, which is valid for nonreduced C. The item statement is unchanged and true; I tested C trivial, G_m in GL_n (K=mu_n) and mu_p in SL_p in characteristic p. Step 1: the faithful-weight-blocks node is used with r=0, which its statement allows, and only its closed-immersion faithful representation is taken; no cycle. Step 2: the item's all-extensions centrality is exactly the new node's commutant hypothesis, so G is block diagonal and C acts by chi_i on each nonzero block, with d_i>=1. Step 3: det from def-sc-general-linear-group; the smooth-connected-derived-subgroup node says maps to the commutative affine G_m are trivial on G^der; this gives a_i^{d_i}=1 as functions on K. Step 4 (elementary): F[GL(V)] surjects onto F[K]=F[G]/(I_C+I_der), and the coordinates map to 0, a_i or 1, so F[t]/(t_i^{d_i}-1) surjects onto F[K] and dim F[K]<=prod d_i. New node diagonalizable-representation-weight-grading: statement-only and self-contained. I checked it is true by the comodule projection argument, including base change and the commutant clause via the universal point in A[M], and on M=0, V=0 and M=Z/p in characteristic p. DAG search (diagonalizable, multiplicative type, D(M), group-like, weight space) found no duplicate. The nearest node, split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition, covers only (G_m)^r. The new node is strictly smaller than the item. No SGA; same-unit theorem citations only; no tool_uses; no fixes.

lean.statement: theorem central_diagonalizable_derived_intersection_finite {F : Type u} [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (G C D : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) [Smooth G.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace G.X.left] [IsAffine G.X.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom] [QuasiCompact G.X.hom] (i : C ⟶ G) (hi : IsClosedSubgroupScheme i.hom.hom) (hcentral : ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra F R] (c : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap F R))) ⟶ C.X) (g : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap F R))) ⟶ G.X), Commute (c ≫ i.hom.hom) g) (hdiag : ∃ (M : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : AddGroup.FG M), Nonempty (C ≅ diagonalizableGroup F M)) (j : D ⟶ G) (hderived : IsDerivedGroupScheme j.hom.hom) : IsFinite (pullback i.hom.hom j.hom.hom).hom
